sector_model: insurer (private mortgage insurance); use earnings, book value, PMIERs sufficiency, default inventory, reserves, holding company debt; no FCF model; GAAP net income with adjusted income shown separately
thesis: National MI writes private mortgage insurance on low down payment loans. After an 11.8% fall to 39.03 on 2026-11-06 (day after Q3 results) it trades at about 7.4x TTM GAAP earnings (392.8M) and 1.08x book value (36.13 per share; 1.02x book excluding unrealized losses), with a 13.8% annualized Q3 ROE, PMIERs available assets of 3.77B versus 2.18B required (173%), insurance in force 229.7B (+5% y/y), buybacks of 2.2M shares in 9M26 and 425M of 6.00% senior notes not due until August 2029.
counterthesis: Earnings power is flat to falling: Q3 net income 93.5M versus 106 Q2 and 96.0M a year earlier, premiums earned 155.5M (down q/q, +3% y/y), new insurance written down 15% q/q, loss ratio rose to 18.7% from 8.3% and 12.3%, new defaults 2,943 (+16% y/y), default inventory 8,571 (+21% y/y) and claim severity 87% versus 73%. The business is a credit cycle bet on U.S. housing and house prices; a downturn would raise defaults and consume PMIERs capital, and GSE or FHFA policy changes can change demand for private MI. A low multiple on peak-like earnings can be a value trap. Book value includes a 400.3M prepaid tax asset (tax and loss bonds) and the stock fell on results, cause not confirmed by any source read. 10-K and call commentary not read.
invalidation: Default inventory rising faster than insured portfolio for two more quarters with loss ratio above 25%; house price declines in key states; PMIERs sufficiency falling below about 130%; GSE policy change reducing MI usage or capital credit; buybacks suspended to preserve capital; new insurance written falling year on year.
